newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Filipino leftist links arrest to APEC summit.
newsitem.headline: Filipino leftist links arrest to APEC summit.

text.p: A top Filipino leftist said on Monday his arrest was intended to cow critics of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit to be held in the Philippines next week.

"This is a desperate attempt by the government to intimidate the workers and the people critical of the harmful things that APEC will bring," Filemon Lagman, chairman of the Coalition of Filipino Workers, told reporters.
Lagman, arrested last week, was to have been formally charged in court with the murder of a policeman in 1992 but the judge postponed the hearing.
"Set me free, President (Fidel) Ramos," the handcuffed Lagman shouted as soldiers with guns hustled him out of the court to a van to be taken to military headquaters where he is being detained.
Dozens of his supporters, with placards reading "Slam Evil, Slam APEC," chanted slogans demanding his release.

Leftist groups say the APEC goal of full trade and investment liberalisation would only benefit industrial countries like the United and Japan and widen disparities between them and less advanced economies.
They also warn that full-scale entry of investments into small Asian countries would ravage the environment.

Despite government denials, political analysts said they believed Lagman's arrest was part of security preparations for the November 25 APEC summit to be held at Subic Bay freeport, northwest of Manila.
The summit will be preceded by meetings in Manila of APEC foreign and trade ministers and senior officials.
Lagman accused the military of fabricating intelligence reports that his supporters would launch terrorist attacks during the summit.
"They are filing charges against a labour leader like me and yet they do not arrest the criminals in government and in the military," Lagman said, referring to corrupt officials.

The intelligence reports indicated that leftists were fomenting unrest among workers in the hotel, telecommunications and transport sectors, which will provide key services to the summit, so they would go on strike and embarrass the government.
